name: Lying Leg Curl
description: The lying leg curl is an isolation exercise for the hamstrings performed on a machine. It trains knee flexion in a prone position, isolating the hamstrings without meaningful hip involvement. It is one of the few exercises that directly isolates the hamstrings and is commonly used as a finishing movement in leg training.

execution.starting_position: Lie face down on the machine with the ankle pad resting on the lower legs just above the heels. Hips flat on the pad, hands gripping the handles.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the ankle pad so it sits comfortably above the Achilles tendon. Align the knee joint with the pivot point of the machine.
steps: Curl the lower legs upward toward the glutes by flexing the knees.
Raise until the lower legs are as vertical as possible.
Lower under control back to full knee extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips off the pad to generate momentum
Stopping short of full range at both the top and bottom
safety_considerations: Ensure the pivot point is aligned with your knee to avoid joint stress
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the bottom, maximum comfortable knee flexion at the top.
coaching_cues: Squeeze your hamstrings hard at the top of each rep
Resist the weight on the way down — the eccentric is as important as the concentric
